subject: Week 48: book the 12-month well visit — the largest vaccine round yet

content.hook: One month to the first birthday: book the 12-month well visit now — the window opens May 10 and the vaccine round is the largest of year one — and start the party decisions that carry multi-week lead times.
content.thisWeek: Standing alone for a few seconds is common this week, and first independent steps are emerging for some — the normal walking range is wide (9–15+ months; CDC checkpoint: 15 months: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). Fine motor consolidates: the pincer grasp is precise for most, and he may squat to pick up a toy and return to standing, stack two blocks, or drop objects into a container. Comprehension runs ahead of speech — expect him to follow simple gesture-plus-word directions, with first words besides mama and dada emerging for some on the same 15-month checkpoint.
watchFors: [low concern] Frequent falls onto his bottom while cruising and standing — normal gait learning; keep hard-edged clutter off the floor.
[monitor] No pointing, waving, or other gestures — document and raise at the 12-month visit.
[monitor] Not pulling to stand or not bearing weight on his legs — same: document, raise at the visit.
[call within 24h] Fever with reduced fluid intake and noticeably fewer wet diapers over a day.
[call now] Labored breathing, blue lips, or unresponsiveness — call 911; do not second-guess.

enrichment.body: Book the first-birthday photographer this week if you want one — SF photographers book 2–4 months out, so remaining May 11 availability is already thin. Candid documentary style beats posed at this age; add a separate 15-minute everyone-in-frame slot or the cake shots will crowd it out.

Decide the party format now and work backward: family-only (6–12 guests, 60–90 minutes, $300–800), mid-size (15–30 guests, $1,500–4,000), or venue event ($5,000+ in SF). Anchor the start time to his nap schedule — morning or early afternoon — and hold everything else to that constraint.
Practice squat-to-pick-up: set a toy on the floor beside furniture he can hold, and let him retrieve it unassisted — the squat-and-rise transition builds the balance that precedes independent steps.
Run stacking and container play daily — two soft blocks and a cup are enough. Putting an object into a container is a 12-month CDC milestone, and stacking trains the wrist control utensils will need.

upcoming: Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster, plus hemoglobin and lead screen. Book it this week; this is the largest single vaccine round of year one.
Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday. Smash-cake bakery orders need 2–3 weeks of lead time; photographer availability is tighter still.
By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — AAP recommends by age 1 or within 6 months of the first tooth; pediatric dentists book weeks out.

subject: Week 49: start bottle weaning now — whole milk arrives at 12 months

content.hook: Start the bottle wean this week: the standard 2–4-week protocol finishes right as whole milk and the open cup take over at 12 months, and the pre-bed bottle is the one worth retiring carefully.
content.thisWeek: First words besides mama and dada are emerging for some — the CDC checkpoint is 15 months — while comprehension surges: he likely follows simple gesture-plus-word directions now (https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). Self-feeding sharpens as the mastered pincer grasp meets early utensil experiments; expect messy but determined spoon work. Cruising, momentary standing, and first steps for some — the wide 9–15+ month walking range holds, and no action is needed either way before the 15-month checkpoint.
watchFors: [low concern] Cup or milk refusal in the first days of a bottle swap — acceptance often takes 10+ exposures; keep offering without pressure.
[low concern] Frustration bursts when a desired object is blocked — toddler-tantrum precursors, on schedule.
[monitor] Refusal of every milk substitute for more than a week, or weight stagnation across the transition.
[call within 24h] Sharply reduced intake with noticeably fewer wet diapers.
[call now] Choking with no air movement, cough, or cry — start back blows and call 911.

enrichment.body: Swap one mid-morning or mid-afternoon bottle for a snack plus milk in a cup this week, then drop roughly one bottle per week — daytime bottles first, the pre-bed bottle last and decoupled from the sleep routine. AAP targets full bottle weaning by 12–18 months; prolonged bottle use tracks with iron deficiency and dental caries.

Practice the open cup at every high-chair meal — a small cup, an ounce of water, your hand steadying his. Drinking from a lidless cup as you hold it is a 12-month CDC milestone, and open-cup skill is the developmental target the sippy cup only postpones.

Play one-step direction games on a daily walk to a familiar destination — say give me the leaf while pointing, then fade the gesture over the week. Following gesture-plus-word directions is the 15-month CDC checkpoint, and comprehension practice now feeds expressive language later.

Order the smash cake from a local bakery now — lead time runs 2–3 weeks and the birthday is under 4 weeks out. A fruit alternative (stacked watermelon rounds with whipped cream) photographs the same with less sugar, if you want to keep year one nearly sugar-free.

upcoming: Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — confirm the booking; MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster, hemoglobin, and lead screen all land here.
Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — bakery cake orders effectively close this week; finalize the guest list alongside.
By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — book now if it is not on the calendar; the AAP by-age-1 window closes with the birthday.

subject: Week 50: first dental visit by age 1 — the AAP deadline is May 11

content.hook: AAP wants a first dental visit by age 1 — that marker is May 11, so book it this week and use the appointment to settle fluoride, bottle-caries, and brushing questions in one pass.
content.thisWeek: Walking confidence grows for those already stepping while others cruise and stand — both on track across the 9–15+ month range (CDC walks-alone checkpoint: 15 months: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). He now uses objects as tools to extend his reach and imitates increasingly elaborate actions — stirring, phone-to-ear, brushing. The gesture repertoire is rich; words besides mama and dada remain emerging for some, with the CDC checkpoint at 15 months.
watchFors: [low concern] Day-to-day food intake swinging 40% in either direction — normal at this age; judge the week, not the meal.
[low concern] Stranger wariness intensifying — expected 12-month social development, not regression.
[monitor] No single words plus minimal babble plus limited response to his name — document the combination and raise it at the 12-month visit.
[call within 24h] New rash within 2 hours of a new food, without any breathing involvement — stop the food and call.
[call now] Fever 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, or hives with facial swelling or breathing difficulty — 911.

enrichment.body: Narrate your daily walk and name everything he points to — point-then-label is the highest-yield language input available right now, and conversational turns, not raw word count, predict later language outcomes.

Keep one weekly participatory music class, or daily singing at home — same active ingredient. Active music beat passive listening on rhythm discrimination and prelinguistic gesture in the one randomized trial at this age; one class is plenty.
Put swim on the year-2 calendar: AAP endorses formal lessons from age 1, which is when the drowning-risk-reduction evidence actually begins — one weekly class, no stacking.

Load meals with iron ahead of the 12-month hemoglobin check — meat, lentils, and iron-fortified cereal with a vitamin C pairing. Iron deficiency peaks at 9–24 months, and excess milk crowding out iron-rich solids is the usual mechanism.

upcoming: By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — AAP recommends by age 1 or within 6 months of the first tooth, whichever comes first.
Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — the largest vaccine round of year one (MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster) plus hemoglobin and lead screen; confirm the slot.
Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — final headcount and food orders next week; keep the party window anchored to naps.

subject: Week 51: birthday final prep — nap-anchored timing and cake-safety rules

content.hook: Ten days out: lock the birthday run-of-show around his naps, set the cake-safety rules before the grandparents arrive, and use the last pre-birthday window for the immersion tour if that is in the year-2 plan.
content.thisWeek: Climbing begins for some — couch cushions and low stairs now register as routes, so audit furniture anchors and stair gates this week. Problem-solving turns visible: he works out how to reach what he wants, uses objects as tools, and follows familiar directions, while words besides mama and dada are still emerging for some (CDC checkpoint: 15 months: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). Walking holds its wide 9–15+ month distribution — steps for many, cruising for the rest, both on track.
watchFors: [low concern] Party-week nap disruption and clinginess around visiting family — expect 2–3 days of recalibration afterward.
[low concern] Climbing attempts — supervise and gate; falls from standing onto flooring are routine, falls from furniture are not.
[monitor] Sustained absence of any specific words by 14–15 months — put it on the 15-month-visit agenda now.
[call within 24h] Fever without an obvious source lasting more than 24 hours.
[call now] Anaphylaxis at the party — hives with lip or facial swelling, or any breathing difficulty after a new food — 911; egg, dairy, and wheat all ride along in most cakes.

enrichment.body: Schedule the party inside an awake window — 10:00–12:00 or 14:00–16:00 — and cap it at 90 minutes. The 16:30–18:00 slot collides with bedtime and reliably produces the meltdown photos.
Serve cake well-mashed or pea-sized, and keep whole grapes, nuts, and popcorn out of reach entirely — then brief the grandparents, who are the usual vector for choking-hazard servings.
Introduce a ring stacker or shape sorter — the right toy for exactly this week: it works the mastered pincer grasp, wrist rotation, and trial-and-error problem-solving in one object.
Tour L'Academy Nob Hill before the birthday if Mandarin immersion is in the year-2 plan and you have not already — entry opens at 12 months and tour-to-start runs 1–3 months.

Announce a book exchange to guests — each brings one children's book instead of a toy. It feeds the nightly read-aloud and heads off the toy influx; 529 contributions cover the relatives who insist on more.

upcoming: Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — window opens May 10; confirm the slot and expect possible mild fever and rash 7–12 days after MMR.
Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — workday plan: small cake on the day, full party the following weekend if that is the format.
By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — last call to book inside the AAP by-age-1 window.

subject: Week 52: year one closes — 12-month visit window opens Monday

content.hook: Year one closes this week: the birthday lands Tuesday and the 12-month well visit window opens Monday — the largest vaccine round of the year plus the hemoglobin and lead screens that close out infancy.
content.thisWeek: The full CDC 12-month checklist is now the frame: pulling to stand, cruising, drinking from a held open cup, the thumb-and-finger pickup, block-in-cup play, waving, calling a parent mama or dada, and pausing at no (https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html) — while independent walking and additional words remain emerging for some, each with a 15-month CDC checkpoint. The year-one ledger, quantified: birth weight has typically tripled by 12 months, length is up roughly 50%, and brain volume has nearly doubled — a growth rate he will never repeat. What the evidence said mattered most this year: conversational turns, sleep consolidation, and iron; what mattered least: everything that promised passive gains. Year two's cadence covers the 15-month visit (DTaP #4, expressive-language takeoff), the 18-month M-CHAT autism screen, and preschool tour season opening September 2027.
watchFors: [low concern] Stranger wariness and clinging at the birthday gathering — expected at 12 months, not a regression.
[low concern] A short fussy crash after the first real cake — for many infants this is the first meaningful sugar exposure; it self-resolves.
[monitor] Multiple absent 12-month milestones — bring the CDC checklist to the well visit rather than waiting for the 15-month one.
[call within 24h] Vomiting or diarrhea persisting past 24 hours after party food.
[call now] Severe respiratory distress, blue lips, or unresponsiveness — 911 before anything else.

enrichment.body: Order the year-1 photo book while the party photos are fresh — 60–100 pages compiled at month 13–14 is the standard build, and the monthly-stack 12-up frame is the other high-yield print.
Carry the 1000-books cadence into year 2 — one book a day clears 1,000 well before kindergarten, and shared reading remains the highest-evidence enrichment line item in the entire portfolio.
Hold the daily outdoor walk at 30+ minutes with him doing more of the moving — new walkers rack up dozens of falls an hour while calibrating, and grass or sand is the ideal practice surface.

Confirm the year-2 activity slate in one sitting: music continues, swim starts now that the AAP evidence window opens at age 1, and nothing else needs adding — the marginal class buys logistics, not development.

upcoming: Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster, hemoglobin, lead screen. Mild fever and rash 7–12 days post-MMR is common and not contagious.
Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — 60–90 minutes, nap-anchored, cake well-mashed; the day is for the adults and the photo record, and that is fine.
By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — the AAP by-age-1 marker passes Tuesday; if unbooked, book now.
